_comment: Curated starter feed packs. Each entry points at an OPML file in this
directory; feed counts are derived from the files at load time, never
stored here, so pruning a dead source does not leave a stale number.
Order is the order the onboarding wizard shows them in.
A committed feed list rots: run scripts/maintenance/audit_feed_packs.py
before a release and prune what it reports as dead.

packs.title: Core
packs.description: The starting point: major security news, government and CERT advisories, NVD and vendor CVE bulletins, the best vendor threat research, and detection-engineering sources. Enough breadth for the engine to show what it does on day one without being a firehose.

packs.title: More news & government
packs.description: The second tier of security press and national CERTs — regional advisories, breach trackers and ransomware leak-site reporting.

packs.title: Vendor advisories
packs.description: Product security bulletins beyond the core set: Linux distributions, industrial and network gear, and the widely deployed open-source projects. High volume, mostly CVE-shaped.

packs.title: Vendor research
packs.description: The long tail of vendor and lab threat research blogs. This is where campaign write-ups, malware analysis and actor attribution come from, and it is the richest source of TTPs and IOCs.

packs.title: Detection engineering
packs.description: Blogs and newsletters focused on building, testing and tuning detections rather than reporting incidents.

packs.title: Detection rule repositories
packs.description: GitHub repositories that publish detection content as code — Sigma, Elastic, Splunk, YARA, Nuclei, Atomic Red Team, LOLBAS and friends. Each commit becomes an entry, which feeds the detection-rule extractor directly.
packs.requires: A GitHub token (Settings → Engine → Enrichment → Keys). Unauthenticated GitHub API calls are capped at 60/hour, which these repositories will exhaust.

packs.title: Practitioner blogs
packs.description: Independent researchers, incident responders and analysts writing under their own name. Lower volume, higher signal, and often the first public account of something.

packs.title: Reddit
packs.description: Security subreddits via each one's hot feed. Useful for early chatter about an exploit or outage, noisier than everything else here.

packs.title: YouTube
packs.description: Conference talks and technical channels. Entries carry the video description and transcript where available, so talks still correlate against your entities.

packs.title: Podcasts
packs.description: Security podcasts, with episode audio playable in the reader.
